description: Figure 3 is a small grouped bar chart illustrating, by year, the distribution of datasets split into “Targeted” versus “Untargeted” (as defined in the caption) across time. The horizontal axis contains the categories as calendar years labeled from 2012 through 2022 in ascending order, with the axis label “Year.” The vertical axis is the value axis labeled “Number of datasets,” shown on a linear scale with tick marks at regular intervals from 0 up to 120. Each year has two adjacent bars: a blue bar for “Targeted” and an orange bar for “Untargeted,” as indicated by the legend titled “Data sources” in the upper-left of the plot. In the early years (2012–2015), both bars are very short (near 0–2 datasets). From 2016 onward, the blue “Targeted” bars increase in height, reaching approximately 10 (2016), about 25 (2017), about 35 (2018), about 50 (2019), about 90 (2020), and peaking around 115 (2021), before dropping to roughly 30 (2022). The orange “Untargeted” bars remain lower throughout, rising to approximately 2 (2016), about 1 (2017), about 2 (2018), about 5 (2019), about 45 (2020), about 50 (2021), and about 10 (2022). The bars are not visually emphasized with annotations or outlines, and the ordering is chronological by year rather than sorted by bar height.
